title: Invertibility of the explicit Koszul quotient product-cone map
statement: Fix the data and one model M from [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum], [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-completion-map]. Suppose v_n is a strict family of chain maps from the intrinsic Koszul tensor tower to the restricted changed-ring ideal-power quotient tower. Require that v_n composed after the Koszul unit is the quotient augmentation, and that every total-tensor summand of nonzero Koszul degree maps to zero. Let w be a map from the Koszul completion complex to the quotient completion complex whose first mapping-cocone coordinate is the first projection followed by product(v_n), and whose degree-minus-one coordinate is the second projection followed by the same product map in the shifted degree. Then localization of w in the derived category is an isomorphism. No construction of v, choice of w, unit conclusion or naturality conclusion is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian Koszul augmentation theorem to the lifted coefficient ring and lifted generators. The ideal agrees with the lift of d.ideal. It gives strict augmentation cones with eventually zero transition maps in the coefficient derived category.

Constant presheaves preserve kernels and cokernels sectionwise, and module sheafification is exact. Thus the additive constant-module functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms, cones and shifts, induces a functor on derived categories and carries the eventual zero cone maps to zero.

The unit and zero-summand conditions uniquely identify v with the tensor augmentation: the Koszul degree-zero unit is invertible and coproduct summands determine maps. Tensor the sheafified coefficient cones with the given K-flat representative. Distribute tensor over the cone summands and multiply the shifted-source summand in tensor degree p by (-1)^p to identify this tensor cone with Cone(v_n). K-flatness preserves acyclic cones, hence quasi-isomorphisms and derived zero maps. Thus the strict cone tower of v is pro-zero. No resolution is chosen in this step: M is already supplied.

Apply the strict derived inverse-limit functor and its pro-zero cone criterion to v. Countable products of pro-etale module sheaves are exact, so localization sends the termwise product cones to derived product cones. Hence the explicit cocones of one minus shift model the strict total derived limits, including their chain-level maps. The two prescribed coordinates of w identify it with this induced map: mapping-cocone projections jointly determine every degree component. It follows that Q(w) is invertible. More explicitly, the strict Roos functor sends a tower to the cocone of one minus shift and sends a map to product(v) on both coordinates. Exact products make it invert quasi-isomorphisms. Resolve towers by K-injective complexes with injective tower terms on the tower site, using prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist. Injectivity of a tower splits each transition, by extending the identity from a finite constant prefix to the next prefix. The recursion y_0=0 and y_(n+1)=σ_n(y_n-x_n) makes one minus shift degreewise surjective, with kernel the strict inverse limit. The inverse-limit-to-Roos map is therefore a quasi-isomorphism on these resolutions. The derived universal property identifies the localized strict Roos functor naturally with RF, including its action on maps. This ensures the two-coordinate strict map is the derived-limit map, rather than an arbitrary triangle filler.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulQuotientCone_isIso (X : Scheme.{t}) (Λ : Type t) [CommRing Λ]
    (d : CompleteCoefficientDatum Λ) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → Λ)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = d.ideal)
    (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory X Λ) (M : AdicKFlatModel X Λ K)
    (v : ∀ n, koszulTensor X Λ r f M.complex n ⟶ adicReductionComplex X d M n)
    (hunit : ∀ n, koszulTensorUnit X Λ r f M.complex n ≫ v n =
      adicReductionAugmentation X d M n)
    (hzero : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), q ≠ 0 →
      HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor M.complex (koszulPowerSheaf X Λ r f n)
        (@curriedTensor _ _ (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (adicConstantRing X Λ)))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q (p + q) rfl ≫ (v n).f (p + q) = 0)
    (hstep : ∀ n, v (n + 1) ≫ adicReductionComplexStep X d M n =
      koszulTensorTransition X Λ r f M.complex n ≫ v n)
    (w : koszulCompletionComplex X Λ r f M.complex ⟶ adicCompletionComplex X d M)
    (hfst : w ≫ adicCompletionProjection X d M =
      CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (koszulOneSubShift X Λ r f M.complex) ≫
        Limits.Pi.map v)
    (hsnd : ∀ p : ℤ, w.f p ≫
      (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (𝟙 _ - adicReductionProductShift X d M)).v
        p (p + -1) rfl =
      (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (koszulOneSubShift X Λ r f M.complex)).v
        p (p + -1) rfl ≫ (Limits.Pi.map v).f (p + -1)) :
    IsIso ((adicLocalization X Λ).map w)
